INTERVENTIONS IN ACTION

One state. Many ways to shape the world.

Control whole objects or selected parts, and explore the scene from different viewpoints. Videos show precomputed results.

CONTINUED CONTROL ACROSS ROLLOUTS

Move the object. Move the camera. Then both.

First, move the excavator with the camera fixed. Next, move the camera while keeping the updated object pose. Finally, control both together. Each rollout continues from the preceding world state.

Object only→Camera only→Object + camera

Left: the world state and prescribed controls. Right: the generated video.

PERSISTENT SCENE CHANGES

Change the scene. Leave. Come back.

The controlled bulldozer pushes a rock. After the updated scene is stored in memory, the camera leaves and revisits the area: the rock remains in its displaced position.

THE CORE IDEA

Memory and intervention, in one shared 3D state.

UniState lifts image latents into 3D to build spatial memory, and expresses object interventions by transforming selected regions within that same memory. The manipulated objects and the surrounding scene remain in a single world-state representation. Rendering this shared state along an independently chosen camera trajectory provides the conditions for video generation.

Scene-Anchored Joint Guidance and Transport-Aligned Augmentation help generated videos follow the specified object motion and camera trajectory.

See the paper for the full method and training details.
